nodes.name: F-doped SnO2 aerogel synthesis
nodes.procedure: SnCl4·5H2O (13.4 mmol, Sigma-Aldrich) was dissolved in a mixture of water and ethanol (3:1, v/v). SnF2 (Sigma-Aldrich) at a specific molar ratio from 0 to 8 mol% was added to the SnCl4 solution, which was then stirred for 1 h. Afterward, the solution was chilled in an ice bath for 20 min, after which chilled propylene oxide (C3H6O, 143 mmol, Sigma-Aldrich) was added dropwise using a syringe. A transparent SnO2 gel was formed after 30 min. Increasing the F-doping concentration turned the gel yellowish. After the gel formation, an excess amount of ethanol was added and the gel was kept in the oven for 3 h at 50°C, during which the solvent was exchanged with fresh deionized water every 1 h. The prepared gel was dried under a CO2 supercritical drying system (R-403, ChemRe System) at a pressure of 110 bar and a temperature of 80°C.

nodes.source_text: EXPERIMENTAL METHODS: Synthesis of SnO2@Pt and F-SnO2@Pt. Undoped and fluorine-doped tin oxide aerogels were synthesized by the epoxide-initiated sol-gel method...

nodes.name: Pt deposition on F-SnO2 aerogel
nodes.procedure: A fixed amount (0.05 g for each coating) of dried F-doped and pristine SnO2 aerogel powders were ground and uniformly spread on a commercially available polypropylene disk (diameter, 50 mm; geometric area, 1,681.5 mm²). Next, Pt was coated on these disks for 120 s at a current of 40 mA using a Pt-sputtering system (Cressington 208HR). During the Pt coating, a homemade wireless controlled vibrator was attached at the bottom of the polypropylene disk. A short pulse (single time) to induce vibration was applied during the deposition process to ensure a highly uniform deposition.

nodes.characterization_summary: SEM images of F-SnO2 aerogel before and after Pt deposition show surface morphology with particle coarsening after Pt coating.
nodes.evidence_snippet: Figure 2a and b shows the scanning electron microscopy (SEM) images before and after the Pt coating on the F-SnO2 aerogel structure via sputtering. Evidently, the particle size of the colloidal particles became larger, indicating particle coarsening.

nodes.characterization_summary: TEM shows typical SnO2 aerogel colloidal structure for F-SnO2.
nodes.evidence_snippet: the transmission electron microscopy (TEM) image in Figure 2c shows a typical SnO2 aerogel colloidal structure.

nodes.characterization_summary: HR-TEM exhibits Pt nanocrystals ~5 nm on F-SnO2 aerogel with Pt(111) spacing of 2.29 Å and SnO2(110) spacing of 3.34 Å.
nodes.evidence_snippet: the HR-TEM image in Figure 2d exhibits the formation of Pt nanocrystals on the F-SnO2 aerogel approximately 5 nm in size with lattice interlayer spacings of Pt(111) and SnO2(110) of 2.29 and 3.34 Å respectively.

nodes.characterization_summary: HAADF-STEM confirms ~5 nm Pt clusters on F-SnO2 aerogel matrix.
nodes.evidence_snippet: High-angle annular dark-field scanning (HAADF)-scanning transmission electron microscopy (STEM) imaging was performed to confirm the deposition of approximately 5 nm Pt clusters on the F-SnO2 aerogel structure.

nodes.characterization_summary: EDX elemental mapping confirms uniform distribution of Pt nanoparticles on F-doped SnO2 aerogel without agglomeration.
nodes.evidence_snippet: the energy-dispersive X-ray spectroscopy (EDX) elemental mapping images shown in Figure 2g-j confirm the uniform distribution of Pt nanoparticles on the F-doped SnO2 aerogel, without agglomeration.

nodes.characterization_summary: Diffuse reflectance spectroscopy shows F-doping increases optical band gap from 3.53 eV to 3.75 eV via Burstein-Moss effect.
nodes.evidence_snippet: Figure 3a shows the spectrum of the optical band gap calculated from a diffuse reflectance spectroscopy (DRS) analysis... Doping the SnO2 aerogel with F significantly increased the optical band gap from 3.53 to 3.75 eV.

nodes.characterization_summary: XRD patterns show rutile-type tetragonal crystal structure with average crystallite size ~3.1 nm for both SnO2@Pt and F-SnO2@Pt.
nodes.evidence_snippet: Figure 3b shows X-ray diffraction (XRD) patterns of SnO2@Pt and F-SnO2@Pt, indicating their rutile-type tetragonal crystal structures... The average crystallite size of both SnO2@Pt and F-SnO2@Pt was approximately 3.1 nm.

nodes.characterization_summary: N2 physisorption shows type IV isotherm with H1 hysteresis; specific surface area 414 m²/g for SnO2@Pt, 321 m²/g for F-SnO2@Pt.
nodes.evidence_snippet: Figure 3c shows the N2 physisorption isotherms of both SnO2@Pt and F-SnO2@Pt with IUPAC type IV with H1 hysteresis... The specific surface area of undoped SnO2@Pt was 414 m²·g⁻¹, which decreased to 321 m²·g⁻¹ after F-doping.

nodes.characterization_summary: XPS Sn 3d shifts to higher binding energy (487.8 eV Sn-F vs 486.7 eV Sn-O); F-doping shifts Pt 4f to higher binding energies indicating metal-support interaction.
nodes.evidence_snippet: doping with F shifts the Sn 3d spectrum toward the higher binding energy side, owing to the higher binding energy of the Sn-F bond (487.8 eV) than that of the Sn-O bond (486.7 eV). Furthermore, F-doping shifts the Pt 4f spectra to higher binding energies.

nodes.characterization_summary: ICP-OES measures Pt contents (wt% and at%) in F-SnO2@Pt with various Pt coating times.
nodes.evidence_snippet: We further examined the Pt contents (wt % and at %) in F-SnO2@Pt with various Pt coating times (Table S1) using inductively coupled plasma optical emission spectroscopy (ICP-OES).

nodes.characterization_summary: SAED shows SnO2 (110), (101), (211) planes and Pt (111) diffraction ring after Pt deposition.
nodes.evidence_snippet: selected area electron diffraction (SAED) patterns show diffracted rings of the (110), (101), and (211) planes in the SnO2 aerogel colloids... After Pt deposition on the aerogel, it was possible to find the (111) diffraction ring pattern of Pt.

nodes.characterization_summary: XANES shows F-doping generates more oxygen vacancies enhancing electron transport.
nodes.evidence_snippet: the X-ray absorption near edge structure (XANES) spectrum was measured to analyze the structural characteristics of F-doped SnO2... The F-doping generated more oxygen vacancies, resulting in an enhanced electron transport ability.
